title: Facial and Upper Extremity Edema
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a pregnant woman at 33 weeks gestation who presents with facial and upper extremity edema, severe hypertension (189/99), new-onset headaches, and blurry vision — signs of end-organ damage. Pre-eclampsia is defined as SBP > 140 or DBP > 90 developing after 20 weeks gestation WITH end-organ dysfunction (proteinuria, visual/cerebral disturbances, pulmonary edema, creatinine > 1.1, elevated LFTs, or thrombocytopenia < 100,000). With SBP > 160, she meets criteria for pre-eclampsia with severe features. Management triad: (1) Magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis to prevent progression to eclampsia, (2) IV labetalol or hydralazine for blood pressure control (labetalol is superior with fewer side effects), (3) Betamethasone for fetal lung maturity if delivering < 34 weeks. Definitive treatment is delivery — with severe features, deliver at ≥ 34 weeks. OB/GYN consult for cesarean section. Admit to ICU or inpatient unit — this is an emergency.

physical_exam.cardiovascular: Severe hypertension (189/99). Assess for pulmonary edema.
physical_exam.neurological: Headache, blurry vision — signs of cerebral end-organ damage. Hyperreflexia may be present.

decoys.label: Nifedipine
decoys.reason_wrong: Can cause reflexive tachycardia and has fetal effects. Not mentioned in ACOG recommendations for pre-eclampsia. Labetalol and hydralazine are preferred.

decoys.label: Expectant management / discharge home
decoys.reason_wrong: Pre-eclampsia with severe features is an emergency. Requires ICU/inpatient management. Delivery is definitive treatment.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: SBP > 160 OR DBP > 110 after 20 weeks + end-organ dysfunction (headache, visual changes, proteinuria, elevated Cr/LFTs, thrombocytopenia). This patient: 189/99 + headache + blurry vision = severe.
Prevents progression to eclampsia. Standard of care for severe pre-eclampsia. Monitor for magnesium toxicity (loss of DTRs, respiratory depression).
First-line antihypertensive for pre-eclampsia. Target SBP < 160 and DBP < 105 (not normal, just safe range).
Promotes fetal lung maturity when delivery anticipated before 34 weeks. 2 doses IM 24h apart.
Definitive treatment = delivery. ≥ 34 weeks: deliver. < 34 weeks: corticosteroids then deliver. Cesarean if unfavorable cervix.

case_summary: Pre-eclampsia with severe features at 33 weeks. BP 189/99 + headache + blurry vision. MgSO4 + IV labetalol + betamethasone + cesarean delivery by OB/GYN. Admit to ICU.
